newsitem.title: DENMARK: Dollar, bonds take fizz out of Danish shares.
newsitem.headline: Dollar, bonds take fizz out of Danish shares.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Monday, dashing expectations that Friday's rally would continue, and dealers expected further falls on Tuesday.

"(Bond) yields and the dollar are in a bad position and the U.S. T-bond has started with a fall of almost a half-point, so at the moment it looks as if the (Danish stock) market will fall further tomorrow," a dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index fell 0.79 point to 159.13 in overall bourse turnover of 1.2 million crowns. The KFX March future fell 0.30 point to 157.40, with 444 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

Dealers blamed the Danske Bank for much of the falling trend. The share dropped nine crowns to 601 after news of its takeover of Sweden's Ostgota Enskilda Bank and rival Unidanmark shed two crowns to 360.

Tele Danmark fell two crowns to 356 on the eve of its 1996 result expected Tuesday. Other companies issuing results on Tuesday include GN Store Nord which closed five up at 695 and ISS which ended the day two crowns higher at 179.
